raw.details:
About the Hackathon

  • BioForge 2026 is a seven-day, on-campus interdisciplinary healthcare innovation hackathon bringing together undergraduate students from Biotechnology, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Biomedical Engineering and allied health-science disciplines.
  • The hackathon aims to transform real-world healthcare challenges into practical, technology-enabled solutions through interdisciplinary collaboration, innovation and industry mentorship.
  • Participants will work on challenges involving scattered health records, missed patient follow-ups, preventive healthcare gaps and post-hospitalisation recovery. Teams will develop working prototypes, computational models or data-driven solutions addressing tangible challenges in healthcare delivery, diagnostics and public health.
  • AssistHealth will contribute industry challenges, insights and mentorship throughout the hackathon.

Challenge Tracks and Problem Statements

Participants can choose one of the following five tracks:

1. AI-Assisted Personal Health Record Organisation

  • Develop an AI-enabled tool that organises medical documents, prescriptions, laboratory reports and consultation summaries into a unified, structured digital health record.

2. Patient Follow-Up and Care Continuity

  • Develop a digital system that identifies missed appointments, pending investigations and overdue follow-ups to help patients stay on track with their treatment.

3. Preventive Healthcare Assessment & Awareness

  • Build a data-driven tool that recommends appropriate preventive health checks based on an individual's age, lifestyle and established clinical guidelines.

4. Post-Hospitalisation Recovery & Monitoring

  • Develop a solution supporting patients after hospital discharge or surgery through follow-up schedules, medication reminders, rehabilitation coordination and recovery tracking.

5. Open-Health Innovation Track

  • Propose an original problem statement addressing a validated gap in clinical workflows, diagnostics, bioinformatics or public health.

Eligibility and Team Structure

  • Open to all undergraduate engineering students across academic years.
  • Inter-college teams and participants from external institutions are welcome.
  • Each team must consist of 3–4 members.
  • At least 2 members must belong to Biotechnology or allied streams, including Biomedical Engineering or Medical Electronics.
  • The remaining 1–2 members may belong to Computer Science, AI/ML or allied engineering streams.
  • Each student may register in only one team.
  • Team rosters will be locked once registration closes.

Registration Fees

  • DSCE Internal Teams: ₹400 per team. Valid DSCE student ID required for all members.
  • External College Teams: ₹500 per team. Valid college ID required for campus entry and verification.

Registration Deadline: 23 November 2026. Exact cutoff time to be confirmed.

Event Schedule

23 November 2026 – Registration Closes
Final deadline for team registration. Team rosters are locked.

24 November 2026 – Kick-Off & Orientation
Inauguration, event briefing, dataset orientation and problem statement finalisation.

24–29 November 2026 – Build Phase
Teams develop their solutions with mentor check-ins and periodic progress reviews.

30 November 2026 – Final Presentations & Finale
Live team demonstrations and pitch presentations to the judging panel, followed by results and prize distribution.

Detailed session timings will be shared with registered teams.

Final Submission Requirements

Each participating team must submit:

  • Presentation deck in PPT or PDF format.
  • Working software/hardware prototype or live demonstration.
  • Public or accessible GitHub repository link, where applicable.
  • Comprehensive README file detailing project architecture, setup instructions and usage.

Prizes and Recognition

1st Place – Winner
₹6,000 worth of gift vouchers + Certificates of Achievement.

1st Runner-Up
₹5,000 worth of gift vouchers + Certificates of Achievement.

2nd Runner-Up
₹4,000 worth of gift vouchers + Certificates of Achievement.

All Participants
Official Certificate of Participation (Soft Copy).

Total prize pool: ₹15,000 worth of gift vouchers.

General Rules and Guidelines

  • All code, models and prototypes must be developed exclusively during the hackathon week (24–30 November 2026).
  • Pre-built projects, reused repositories and previously submitted competition work are prohibited.
  • Teams must use open-access datasets and comply with dataset licences and terms of use.
  • Open-source libraries, APIs and frameworks are permitted with appropriate attribution.
  • Generative AI tools may be used, but their usage must be disclosed and participants must be able to explain every component of their solutions.
  • Attendance at scheduled mentor check-ins is mandatory.
  • Sensitive health, clinical and biological records must be anonymised.
  • Presentations must address algorithmic bias, data privacy and patient safety.
  • Prototypes are proof-of-concept demonstrations and must not be represented as clinically validated tools or medical advice.
  • Plagiarism, harassment, discrimination and disruptive behaviour may result in disqualification.
  • Judging panel decisions are final and binding.

Event Coordinators

Assistant Professor, Department of Biotechnology, DSCE.

Assistant Professor, DSCE.

Student Organising Team, BioForge 2026.

Event Venue

CIL Unit 1, Dr. CD Sagar Centre for Life Sciences, Dayananda Sagar College of Engineering (DSCE), 1st Stage, Kumaraswamy Layout, Bengaluru, Karnataka – 560111.

Forge Ideas. Build Solutions. Transform Healthcare.
